title: ‘Making sure that people are in a good place is draining, and nobody does that for me’: the pandemic and its ongoing impact on teachers and headteachers
text_snippet: ‘Making sure that people are in a good place is draining, and nobody does that for me’: the pandemic and its ongoing impact on teachers and headteachers Introduction Due to the Covid−19 pandemic, education provision was significantly disrupted for two academic years. Schools saw an increase in their workload and scope of their responsibilities which impacted staff members physically, mentally and professionally. This study examines how the pandemic and school disruptions impacted teachers and other staff members, and their continued experience since all restrictions have been lifted. Methods Twenty-three staff members were interviewed in the 2021/2022 academic year and nine staff members in the 2023/2024 academic year using semi-structured online interviews. Results Results showed that the pandemic was challenging for staff members with their well-being and workload significantly affected. Even though restrictions in England were lifted in the summer of 2021, staff members are still struggling with the effects of the pandemic, as well as emerging post-pandemic challenges such as the cost-of-living crisis. Discussion Findings from these interviews suggest that the impact of the pandemic has been long-term and highlight the need to include staff members in any discussions regarding recovery plans. title: From information providers to learning designers: heutagogical teaching practices in AI-enhanced education
text_snippet: From information providers to learning designers: heutagogical teaching practices in AI-enhanced education Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has intensified longstanding questions about teachers' roles and the pedagogical conditions under which technology supports learner autonomy. This qualitatively driven embedded mixed-methods study examined practices reported and represented by Israeli teachers during an eight-week professional development program on AI, self-regulated learning, and learner-centered pedagogy. The primary qualitative strand drew on reflections, open-ended questionnaire responses, lesson plans, and pedagogical artifacts and used a hybrid deductive-inductive analysis. An exploratory quantitative strand compared 61 consenting pre-program submissions with 26 consenting post-program submissions. Because submissions were anonymous and unlinked, Welch independent-samples tests were used. Post-program means were descriptively higher for reflective teaching, AI-supported planning, and inquiry-oriented design, and essentially unchanged for differentiated instruction; none of the four comparisons was statistically significant after Holm adjustment. title: Exploring primary teachers’ emotional and instructional challenges in supporting students with general reading difficulties in Saudi Arabia
text_snippet: Exploring primary teachers’ emotional and instructional challenges in supporting students with general reading difficulties in Saudi Arabia Introduction This study investigates the instructional and emotional challenges primary school teachers face when teaching students with general reading difficulties in Saudi Arabia. Methods The study employed a descriptive phenomenological design to examine teachers' lived experiences of addressing reading difficulties. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 14 primary school teachers who varied in experience, age, and sex. The data were analyzed using an inductive, data-driven thematic analysis. Results The analysis generated four themes: (a) instructional challenges, (b) emotional and affective challenges, (c) instructional adaptations, and (d) school preparedness and professional develop The findings provide valuable insights into the importance of professional development and educational resources in supporting students with reading difficulties. They also highlight the vital role of primary school teachers in assisting these students and the consequent impact of this responsibility on teachers' workloads. title: Design and exploratory assessment of a mobile educational prototype for Saraguro cultural heritage and Kichwa-language learning
text_snippet: Design and exploratory assessment of a mobile educational prototype for Saraguro cultural heritage and Kichwa-language learning Introduction Digital resources can broaden access to living heritage, but their contribution depends on cultural relevance, community governance, and claims that remain proportional to the evidence collected. This study reports the design and exploratory assessment of a mobile educational prototype focused on Saraguro cultural heritage and introductory Kichwa-language learning. The prototype organized multimedia content on gastronomy, rituals and festivals, handicrafts, ancestral medicine, stories, cultural places, and basic Kichwa expressions with audio-playback controls. It was informed by a previous project website, saragurotradiciones.site, but the two resources were technically distinct and only the mobile prototype was assessed. Methods The development process was organized through the five Mobile-D phases. An exploratory qualitative evaluation involved 12 purposively selected participants: five undergraduate students, three local tour guides, two cultural-tourism operators, and two educators. title: Teachers' evaluations of evidence— accurate statistical understanding but biased relevance perceptions
text_snippet: Teachers' evaluations of evidence— accurate statistical understanding but biased relevance perceptions To realize evidence-informed school practice, teachers need to critically evaluate scientific findings, drawing on, among other factors, their attitudes and their educational research literacy. However, evaluating such findings is a complex process that can be distorted by different cognitive biases, such as anchoring effects. Preliminary research has shown that some aspects of teachers' evaluation of research are heavily biased, while others are quite accurate. Against this backdrop, this study aims to investigate the extent to which anchoring effects shape different components of teachers' evaluations of evidence. Based on dual-process theories, relevance perceptions might be influenced by intuitive processing (System 1), which is why we hypothesize that willingness-to-pay ratings as a proxy for relevance perceptions are susceptible to anchoring effects. In contrast, effect magnitude estimates might be formed by deliberate reasoning processes (System 2) and thus remain unaffected. To test these hypotheses, we conducted two experimental studies with N 1 = 119 and N 2 = 90 English-speaking teachers from the US. title: Data collection and analysis for neurodevelopmental disorders: a single-case study and tutorial for clinicians and educators
text_snippet: Data collection and analysis for neurodevelopmental disorders: a single-case study and tutorial for clinicians and educators It is generally acknowledged that optimizing teaching and learning is best accomplished with real-time data and rapid analysis and feedback. This is perhaps especially true for individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders whose highly individualized learning profiles make standardized approaches insufficient. However, for the vast majority of such individuals, practical limitations limit the accomplishment of this ideal. Here, we present a fully implemented approach to data-driven interventions, developed and tested in a home-based, full-time hybrid clinical-educational program for an individual with autism (level 3). The system encourages real-time data recording with minimum interference with ongoing activities, and a data analysis and reporting pipeline grounded on freely available software that does not require extensive statistical knowledge. This system could potentially be a base for others to build on and modify for specific situations and needs.

title: Influence of AI tools across research processes on the research productivity of postgraduate students in Nigerian public universities
text_snippet: Influence of AI tools across research processes on the research productivity of postgraduate students in Nigerian public universities Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming research practices in higher education, yet empirical evidence on how AI supports research productivity among students remains limited, particularly in developing contexts. This study examined the influence of AI tools used during the research preparation, analysis, and dissemination stages on the research productivity of postgraduate students in public universities in Nigeria. The study was guided by the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) and Experiential Learning Theory. Methods The study adopted a descriptive survey design involving 312 respondents. Data were collected using the AI Tools Utilisation and Research Productivity Questionnaire (AITURPQ) and analysed using simple linear regression. The analysis examined the predictive effects of AI-assisted research preparation, analytical, and dissemination tools on research productivity. Results The findings reveal that AI-assisted research preparation tools significantly predicted research productivity (R² = .241, p < .05). title: A framework for authentic assessment in legal and ethical business curricula
text_snippet: A framework for authentic assessment in legal and ethical business curricula Introduction Legal and Ethical Business (LEB) curricula in higher education (HE) are traditionally taught through lectures and subsequently assessed via invigilated examinations. These methods have been shown to result in suboptimal student engagement, with challenges to students inculcating the desired theoretical knowledge. Studies have shown that authentic assessment (AA) offers a viable alternative towards enhancement of student learning, engagement, and skill development while maintaining academic integrity. This study proposes an authentic assessment practical framework for LEB. The proposed framework may support the adoption of AA in LEB curricula and in turn have a positive impact on student learning in higher education. Methods A systematic literature review (SLR) was employed to identify, evaluate, and synthesise existing research on the topic. The review followed a structured search, screening and categorisation process to develop the proposed evidence-informed framework for AA. title: A methodology for AI-supported cross-level professional collaboration in computer science education using the AI-Ustaz platform
text_snippet: A methodology for AI-supported cross-level professional collaboration in computer science education using the AI-Ustaz platform Introduction Contemporary educational environments require educators to participate in professional networks that extend across institutional levels. This study presents a methodology for AI-supported cross-level professional collaboration involving pre-service teachers, secondary-school teachers, and college instructors, with the AI-Ustaz platform serving as the shared technological environment. Methods The methodology comprised three sequential stages: theoretical–orientational, technological, and project–networked. A cluster quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was implemented during the 2024–2025 academic year with 347 participants across nine educational institutions in Kazakhstan. Participants were allocated to an experimental group (n = 178) and a control group (n = 169). Cognitive, performative, and reflective components of networked-collaboration competence were assessed. Results Descriptive analyses indicated greater pretest-to-posttest improvements in the experimental group across the cognitive, performative, and reflective components. At posttest, the experimental group required approximately 61% less time to prepare instructional materials than the control group

title: Generative AI as a catalyst for critical thinking: reframing students from consumers to co-creators
text_snippet: Generative AI as a catalyst for critical thinking: reframing students from consumers to co-creators This study examined students’ AI literacy, perceived learning benefits, and ethical awareness following participation in a structured, AI-integrated classroom activity. The study also investigated the relationships among these constructs and examined whether perceived learning benefits mediate the relationship between AI literacy and ethical awareness. In addition, the study explored whether students’ responses differed according to gender, prior AI experience, and frequency of AI use. The study involved 104 undergraduate students who participated in a hands-on classroom activity over two academic semesters. Students used generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot, to prepare and deliver short lessons to their classmates, followed by discussions addressing responsible and ethical AI use. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring AI literacy, perceived learning benefits, ethical awareness, and related aspects of students’ experiences. title: From journal validation to quality governance: a policy analysis of India's transition from UGC-CARE to quality-oriented research assessment and its implications for medical and dental education
text_snippet: From journal validation to quality governance: a policy analysis of India's transition from UGC-CARE to quality-oriented research assessment and its implications for medical and dental education Background The University Grants Commission (UGC) announced the discontinuation of the UGC-CARE Reference List through a Public Notice dated 11 February 2025, following the Commission's decision taken at its 584th meeting on 3 October 2024, marking a major shift in India's approach to research quality governance. Introduced in 2019 to address predatory publishing, the UGC-CARE framework provided a centralized mechanism for identifying credible publication venues. The transition to quality-oriented research assessment emphasizing publication ethics, peer review integrity, editorial transparency, and institutional accountability has generated considerable debate, yet its implications for research integrity and health professions education remain insufficiently explored. Methods A narrative policy analysis was conducted using publicly available UGC policy documents, regulatory reports, international responsible research assessment frameworks, and peer reviewed literature. Guided by Walt and Gilson's Policy Analysis Triangle, the analysis examined the policy context, content, process, and key actors associated with India's transition from the UGC-CARE framework to quality-oriented rese

title: Not all body percussion is equal: alignment and temporal cue weight in second language phonology
text_snippet: Not all body percussion is equal: alignment and temporal cue weight in second language phonology Body percussion, the intentional production of sound through clapping, patting, stamping, and snapping, is among the most widely used embodied techniques in language classrooms; however, no theoretical account specifies how a rhythmic bodily action might become a phonological representation available for speech production. This study addresses this gap. title: An NLP-assisted and explainable rule-based platform for formative feedback from academic similarity reports
text_snippet: An NLP-assisted and explainable rule-based platform for formative feedback from academic similarity reports Introduction Academic similarity reports identify textual overlap but do not, by themselves, determine plagiarism or explain how students should revise their writing. This study describes an implemented, explainable, teacher-mediated workflow and reports a preliminary feasibility-oriented assessment of teacher-perceived usefulness. Methods The platform processed information from 200 real, deidentified undergraduate similarity-report cases from a single institution. Fifteen instructors reviewed editable feedback drafts through a web interface and selected Accept, Review, or Redo, mapped analytically to Correct, Partial, or Adjust. Case-level exploratory analyses examined associations between teacher ratings and recorded severity, operational issue category, source type, similarity percentage, and number of sources. Results Correct, Partial, and Adjust ratings were recorded for 65 (32.5%), 75 (37.5%), and 60 (30.0%) cases, respectively. Correct plus Partial represented 140 cases (70.0%) as an aggregate indicator of initial-draft usability, not system accuracy. title: Family cultural capital and academic achievement in a smaller-city Chinese high-school context: evidence from Linfen
text_snippet: Family cultural capital and academic achievement in a smaller-city Chinese high-school context: evidence from Linfen Purpose Family cultural capital is an established explanation of educational inequality, and its relationship with academic achievement has been examined in previous Chinese research. Rather than proposing a new cultural-capital construct, this study provides an extension by examining the relative associations of cultural resources, parental education level and parent-child communication with academic achievement among high school students in Linfen, Shanxi Province. Methodology The study focuses on a smaller-city educational setting that has received less attention than national datasets and major metropolitan contexts in the literature considered here. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was administered to 200 students aged 16–18 from two high schools in Linfen, Shanxi Province, selected through stratified cluster sampling. Academic achievement was measured using students’ reported end-of-term performance across three municipal examination subjects. title: What is a green school? Understanding stewardship, well-being, and sustainability education
text_snippet: What is a green school? Understanding stewardship, well-being, and sustainability education This research article examines the notion of the green school through the lens of health and wellness; outdoors education; and stewardship of resources. The article first overviews the framework of the U.S. Department of Education Green Ribbon Schools (ED-GRS) recognition which includes the three green pillars of reducing environmental impacts , areas of facilities, transportation, grounds and operations; improving health and wellness through coordinated school health, with consideration to air quality, learning environment, school nutrition, and outdoors physical activity; and offering effective environmental and sustainability education that emphasizes hands-on, real-world learning, civic engagement, and STEM. We provide a brief descriptive analysis of the 769 ED-GRS award recipients over a 13 year period that spans 585 schools, 123 districts, and 60 postsecondary institutions. Our analysis yields insights on potential gaps that have emerged in practice. title: Rebuilding through science: a hybrid STEMM recovery model for higher education reconstruction in Gaza
text_snippet: Rebuilding through science: a hybrid STEMM recovery model for higher education reconstruction in Gaza This review examines the role of science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and medicine (STEMM) education in the long-term reconstruction of Gaza following the extensive destruction of its higher education system since 2023. Evidence is drawn from institutional assessments, peer-reviewed research on higher education in Gaza, and comparative studies of other conflict-affected systems, including Syria, Afghanistan, Ukraine, and Sudan. Quantitative indicators are drawn from four source families employing methodologically distinct procedures, namely satellite and field-based damage assessment, an interim damage assessment applying rapid damage and needs assessment methodology, national statistical survey, and administrative casualty records reported by the Palestinian Ministry of Education and Higher Education, with points of divergence, single-source indicators, and remaining verification limits reported explicitly. title: Problem solving and responsible GenAI use in assessment: students’ reported experiences in open and distance learning
text_snippet: Problem solving and responsible GenAI use in assessment: students’ reported experiences in open and distance learning Introduction Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used by students to obtain explanations, generate ideas, improve written responses and prepare assessment tasks. However, limited evidence exists on how students in open-distance alternative-access programmes experience GenAI in mathematics assessment. Methods This qualitative study examined how 27 Higher Certificate students at a South African open and distance learning institution described the role, benefits and limitations of GenAI while preparing fraction-related portfolio activities. Data were collected via a single open-ended questionnaire item, completed voluntarily after all assessment activities had been submitted. The responses were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Four overlapping themes were identified: support for understanding and approaching tasks, support for constructing written responses, conditional trust and evaluative engagement, and non-use, resistance and ambiguous engagement. title: Interactive effects of supervisory styles and institutional contexts on the practical innovation ability of professional degree postgraduates
text_snippet: Interactive effects of supervisory styles and institutional contexts on the practical innovation ability of professional degree postgraduates Introduction As the global knowledge economy increasingly demands high-level applied talents, cultivating practical innovation ability has become a priority for professional degree postgraduate education. Drawing on the Componential Theory of Creativity and Resource Dependence Theory, this study conceptualized practical innovation ability as a multidimensional construct integrating innovation knowledge, skills, thinking, disposition, and performance. Methods Using survey data from 3,338 professional degree postgraduates across 20 Chinese universities, this study employed two-way analyses of variance to examine how supervisory styles interacted with university level and university type in shaping practical innovation ability. Results The results revealed significant interactions between supervisory styles and institutional characteristics. Specifically, regarding university level, in non-Double First-Class universities where systemic resources are relatively scarce, a supportive style functioned as a vital compensatory resource. title: Perceived educational value, ethical risk, and support for responsible AI governance in higher education: an embedded mixed-methods study
text_snippet: Perceived educational value, ethical risk, and support for responsible AI governance in higher education: an embedded mixed-methods study Introduction Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is becoming increasingly embedded in higher education assessment, yet the perceptual factors that motivate stakeholder support for its institutional governance remain underexamined. This study investigated the extent to which Perceived Educational Value (PEV) and AI Ethical Risk Perception (AERP) are associated with Responsible AI Governance Support (RAGS) among higher education stakeholders. Methods An embedded mixed-methods survey design was employed. Quantitative Likert-scale data and qualitative open-ended responses were collected concurrently through one structured questionnaire; full-sample quantitative analyses were conducted first, followed by thematic analysis of the open-ended responses to contextualize and deepen interpretation of the quantitative findings. A structured questionnaire was administered to 192 participants (125 students and 67 instructors) recruited from public and private higher education institutions in the United Arab Emirates, with N = 192 yielding statistical power exceeding.99 for the structural model. title: The B-AIMT: development and initial validation of a domain-specific instrument for assessing mathematics teachers’ beliefs about artificial intelligence
text_snippet: The B-AIMT: development and initial validation of a domain-specific instrument for assessing mathematics teachers’ beliefs about artificial intelligence This study presents the development of the Belief Scale for Artificial Intelligence in Mathematics Teaching (B-AIMT) and provides psychometric evidence for its initial validation as a domain-specific instrument assessing teachers’ beliefs about AI in mathematics instruction. Based on data from 442 German pre-service and in-service teachers, confirmatory factor analyses provided support for a theoretically grounded multidimensional belief structure comprising nine latent belief dimensions organized within two overarching domains: beliefs about student mathematics learning with AI and beliefs about mathematics teaching with AI. The resulting subdimensions capture perceived instructional affordances, epistemic potentials, perceived risks, and ethical considerations related to AI systems. The final measurement model showed satisfactory model fit and good internal consistency. Measurement invariance analyses supported scalar invariance across pre-service and in-service teachers, allowing meaningful comparisons of latent means. title: Teaching coherence and cohesion to Chinese EFL undergraduates: a concept-based classroom intervention
text_snippet: Teaching coherence and cohesion to Chinese EFL undergraduates: a concept-based classroom intervention Despite the importance of coherence and cohesion to effective writing, few studies have examined how these concepts can function as a psychological tool for thinking and writing. To advance this line of inquiry, we presented a mixed-methods research that employed the Concept-based Language Instruction (C-BLI) to teach coherence and cohesion to Chinese English as Foreign Language (EFL) learners, with an aim to examine changes in learners' conceptual understandings and writing performance following the intervention. Data sources included written texts, metalinguistic knowledge tests as well as learning process data from four focal students. Quantitative pretest-posttest comparisons revealed substantial improvements in learners' conceptual understanding, whereas no statistically significant changes were observed in overall writing quality or coherence and cohesion. Qualitative analyses of the focal students’ learning data showed that the learners drew on their knowledge repertoire and metaphorical thinking to appropriate the target concepts. title: School leadership mentoring across four European educational contexts: an exploratory qualitative study
text_snippet: School leadership mentoring across four European educational contexts: an exploratory qualitative study Over the past decades, school leadership has become a central element in educational reform, school improvement, and organizational effectiveness across education systems worldwide. Nevertheless, European education systems continue to reflect diverse governance arrangements shaped by national trajectories and institutional legacies. Although school leadership is widely recognized as a key determinant of educational effectiveness, comparatively limited research has examined how mentoring for school leaders is configured within distinct governance contexts. Addressing this gap, this study undertakes an analysis of six leadership trajectories from four European countries selected for their contrasting governance orientations: Portugal and Spain as cases reflecting traditions that tend to be more centralized, and Belgium and the Netherlands as cases characterized by a tendency toward greater decentralization and stronger school-level autonomy. title: Concrete reading theory: embodied anchors for early literacy in digital contexts
text_snippet: Concrete reading theory: embodied anchors for early literacy in digital contexts Background Foundational literacy models have long privileged visual–auditory decoding pathways, systematically marginalising the haptic, proprioceptive, and affective systems that evolutionarily predate symbolic processing. The accelerating digital transformation of early childhood has compounded this problem by replacing hands-on, material engagement with screen-mediated interaction, raising urgent questions about the sensorimotor foundations of orthographic learning. Hypothesis/theory We propose Concrete Reading Theory (CRT), a neurocognitive framework positing that durable literacy acquisition is hypothesised to depend on functional anchors—multisensory, affectively charged cognitive structures that bind abstract orthographic symbols to concrete sensorimotor networks. “Concrete” refers not to physical materials alone but to the neurocognitive act of concretising: grounding arbitrary symbols in embodied experience. title: Social belonging and academic mindset affect student performance in an introductory biology course at a two-year college
text_snippet: Social belonging and academic mindset affect student performance in an introductory biology course at a two-year college Introduction Access-oriented institutions serve increasingly diverse student populations and play an important role in broadening participation in STEM. However, relatively little research has studied how affective factors contribute to student success in introductory STEM courses, specifically Introductory Biology, within these settings. This study examined how the affective constructs of social belonging (sense of belonging and belonging uncertainty) and academic mindset (entity and incremental beliefs) relate to student performance in Introductory Biology at a U.S. two-year institution. Methods Survey and exam data were collected across 16 course sections ( N = 310). Theory-driven hierarchical and multiple regressions models, controlling for academic preparation, were used to examine relationships among affective variables and performance. Because these affective variables are underexplored in these contexts, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were conducted and supported the expected two-factor structures for both measures. title: Scientific and methodological foundations for teaching physicochemical analysis methods in continuous chemical education: a scoping review
text_snippet: Scientific and methodological foundations for teaching physicochemical analysis methods in continuous chemical education: a scoping review Background Rapid technological advancement, digitalization of analytical instrumentation, and the growing demand for interdisciplinary competence have significantly transformed the role of analytical chemistry in science and industry. These changes necessitate a systematic reconsideration of how physicochemical analysis methods are taught within continuous chemical education. Objective This scoping review aimed to map and systematize the structural components of modern analytical chemistry education, identify dominant pedagogical approaches, and conceptualize their functional interrelationships within an integrated educational framework. Design/methods The study was conducted as a scoping review in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search was performed in Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, ACS Publications, SpringerLink, and RSCI (eLIBRARY.ru), covering publications from 1975 (the earliest eligible record retrieved) to 2024. Eligible studies addressed pedagogical, curricular, or methodological aspects of teaching analytical chemistry or physicochemical analysis methods. title: AI-TPACK readiness and generative AI integration among mathematics lecturers in Ghana's public colleges of education: predictors of AI-TPACK readiness
text_snippet: AI-TPACK readiness and generative AI integration among mathematics lecturers in Ghana's public colleges of education: predictors of AI-TPACK readiness Despite growing interest in artificial intelligence (AI) in education, empirical evidence on AI-extended Technological Pedagogical and Content Knowledge (AI-TPACK) readiness and generative AI integration among mathematics lecturers remains limited, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. This study examined AI-TPACK readiness and generative AI integration among mathematics lecturers in Ghana's public Colleges of Education and investigated whether AI literacy, self-efficacy in AI use, and teaching experience predicted AI-TPACK readiness. A cross-sectional survey design was employed with 214 mathematics lecturers from 49 public Colleges of Education in Ghana. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire measuring AI-TPACK readiness, generative AI integration practices, AI literacy, self-efficacy in AI use, and teaching experience. Descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression were used to analyse the data. The findings showed that overall AI-TPACK readiness was moderate (M = 2.48, SD = 0.71). title: Do you prefer UDL? Bridging the gap between students and faculty in the implementation of universal design for learning in higher education
text_snippet: Do you prefer UDL? Bridging the gap between students and faculty in the implementation of universal design for learning in higher education The consolidation of inclusive education in higher education has driven the adoption of Universal Design for Learning (UDL) as a framework for promoting more accessible, flexible, and equitable environments. However, questions remain regarding the degree of alignment between the inclusive strategies implemented by faculty and student preferences. The objective of this study was to conduct a comparative analysis of university students’ preferences and faculty members’ reported application of teaching strategies based on UDL. A quantitative, cross-sectional, non-experimental, and comparative study was conducted. A total of 196 participants took part (170 students and 26 faculty members). A structured questionnaire on effective strategies for inclusive higher education aligned with the UDL was used, consisting of 37 items grouped into six dimensions. The instrument demonstrated adequate levels of internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranging from.78 to.89 for students and from.72 to.85 for faculty members. title: Design and evaluation of a novel digital teaching and learning process for higher education: a proof-of-concept study
text_snippet: Design and evaluation of a novel digital teaching and learning process for higher education: a proof-of-concept study Introduction Digital transformation in higher education has increased the demand for instructional approaches that promote learner engagement, inclusivity, information literacy, and self-directed learning. Although microlearning, Universal Design for Learning (UDL), and constructive alignment have individually demonstrated educational benefits, limited research has explored their integration within a unified pedagogical framework. This study designed and evaluated a novel digital teaching and learning process that integrates microlearning, connective alignment, and the principles of UDL to enhance teaching and learning in higher education. Methods To evaluate the impact of the novel digital teaching and learning process, a case study was conducted in the “Evidence-Based Practice in Physiotherapy” course in the BSc in Physiotherapy curriculum. A mixed-methods proof-of-concept study employing a randomized crossover design was conducted to evaluate the academic effectiveness, the students’ perceptions of the teaching, and the students’ satisfaction. title: Human-written and AI-generated revisions: an appraisal analysis of dialogic positioning in argumentative writing
text_snippet: Human-written and AI-generated revisions: an appraisal analysis of dialogic positioning in argumentative writing Introduction This study presents a systematic comparative analysis of appraisal resource use across human-written and AI-generated texts. Drawing on Appraisal Theory, with a focus on Engagement, it compares first drafts, peer-feedback revisions, and AI-generated revisions, which were produced by ChatGPT-4 based on students’ first drafts using a standardized prompt. Method To conduct the comparison, a corpus of 168 essays across the three draft types was compiled based on four writing tasks completed by undergraduate English majors in China. All drafts were manually coded and data were analyzed using linear mixed models and descriptive statistics. Results First, AI-generated revisions employed significantly more appraisal resources than peer-feedback revisions, which in turn exceeded first drafts. The increases were primarily driven by Attitude and Graduation resources, while the frequency of Engagement resources remained stable across all three draft types. title: Gender differences in attitudes toward disability among university students in health and education programs
text_snippet: Gender differences in attitudes toward disability among university students in health and education programs Introduction Positive attitudes toward disability are essential for promoting inclusive educational and healthcare practices. However, evidence remains inconclusive regarding how gender, academic discipline, and previous contact with people with disabilities shape these attitudes among university students. The aim of this study was to examine whether attitudes toward disability differ according to gender, degree program, and previous contact with people with disabilities among university students enrolled in health and education degrees. A secondary aim was to explore whether the factors underlying favourable attitudes differ by gender using classification tree analysis. Methods A cross-sectional comparative study was conducted involving 446 university students from Extremadura, pursuing degrees in Physical Activity and Sport Science, Occupational Therapy, and Early Childhood Education, participated in this comparative research. To assess their attitudes, the Spanish Attitudes Toward People with Disabilities Scale for Professionals was administered to both first year and final year students. title: Impact of virtual and hands-on laboratory experimentation on the acquisition of conceptual science knowledge: a meta-analysis
text_snippet: Impact of virtual and hands-on laboratory experimentation on the acquisition of conceptual science knowledge: a meta-analysis Introduction Hands-on laboratory experimentation is an important contributor to the successful acquisition of conceptual science knowledge, but its practical application has several limitations. Virtual laboratory experiments help overcome most of these shortcomings and may also be more effective than hands-on laboratory activities in promoting conceptual science knowledge acquisition. Methods In this study, the impact of virtual and hands-on laboratory experimentation on the acquisition of conceptual science knowledge was compared by means of a meta-analysis. The meta-analysis encompassed 43 studies selected according to the predefined inclusion criteria, and the principles of Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses procedure. For each study, one effect size value of Hedges' g was calculated. Subsequently, due to their heterogeneity, the overall effect size value was computed through the use of the random-effects model. title: Peer review contributions as a measure of academic distinction requirements of faculty promotion committees: rapid review of top-ranking universities
text_snippet: Peer review contributions as a measure of academic distinction requirements of faculty promotion committees: rapid review of top-ranking universities Introduction Journal peer review expertise is a cornerstone of academic practice. However, research publication productivity often overshadows prepublication peer review as a marker of academic distinction. The objective of this review is to examine the status of peer review contributions as a criterion of academic performance within faculty promotion committees at leading universities. Methods We reviewed handbooks, guidelines, and procedures related to faculty promotion and tenure on the official websites of the top 50 universities ranked by the QS World University Rankings 2025. Peer review, as a requirement of academic promotion, was identified and reported if it fell within the scope of, a) peer review reporting or authoring, b) peer review education or mentoring, or c) peer review training or learning. The primary assessment criteria governing academic promotion were reported. Results Eight universities were excluded due to unavailable or inaccessible information on their websites, and 42 were included in the final analysis. title: Collaboration as an effective tool for the implementation of the Lesotho inclusive education policy 2018: opportunities and challenges
text_snippet: Collaboration as an effective tool for the implementation of the Lesotho inclusive education policy 2018: opportunities and challenges Background The implementation of the Lesotho Inclusive Education Policy 2018 is complex and requires a collaborative approach. Given the complexity of inclusive education, the paper acknowledges that there must be participation of different role players in helping teachers to effectively carry the mandate of the policy. Aims The study aims to explore how collaboration is effective in supporting the education of Learners with Special Education Needs (LSEN) through the perspectives and experiences of teachers and provides a comprehensive evidence-based approaches for improving the implementation of inclusive education policies through a collaborative approach. Methods The paper is framed within ecological systems theory to understand how collaboration as premised on the LIEP 2018 could effectively help the implementation phase of the policy. The paper is lensed under the interpretive paradigm and designed with a qualitative research approach. Nine teachers were purposively selected from a regular school and were engaged in a focus group discussion. title: Active pedagogical approaches in physical education across school and higher-education contexts and in physical education teacher education: a systematic review of pedagogical models, outcomes and implementation conditions (2005–2025)
text_snippet: Active pedagogical approaches in physical education across school and higher-education contexts and in physical education teacher education: a systematic review of pedagogical models, outcomes and implementation conditions (2005–2025) Background Physical Education (PE) and Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) increasingly use student-centred pedagogical approaches, but evidence from learner-oriented PE contexts and professional teacher education is often synthesised together. This systematic review examined active pedagogical approaches in PE and PETE between 2005 and 2025, focusing on pedagogical models, learner and professional outcomes, and implementation conditions. Methods Searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, ERIC, SPORTDiscus and PubMed in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Three reviewers independently conducted study selection, data extraction and MMAT appraisal, resolving discrepancies by consensus. The protocol was not prospectively registered. Owing to substantial contextual and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively rather than meta-analytically. title: Making mathematical reasoning visible: a qualitative comparative case study of students’ reasoning, representation, and communication
text_snippet: Making mathematical reasoning visible: a qualitative comparative case study of students’ reasoning, representation, and communication Developing students’ capacity for mathematical reasoning and communication is a central goal of contemporary mathematics education, yet qualitative evidence on how these competencies are externalized during problem solving remains limited. This study investigates how students’ mathematical reasoning, use of representations, and modes of engagement differ in the ways 19 they become visible during problem solving, even when solutions are mathematically correct. Adopting a qualitative comparative case study design, three secondary school students exhibiting contrasting modes of engagement were examined while solving a non-routine algebraic problem designed to elicit representational transitions and justification. Data were drawn from written solution artefacts and follow-up semi-structured, artifact-based interviews. Thematic analysis focused on reasoning documentation, representational coordination, and forms of mathematical communication, emphasizing processes of externalization rather than evaluative correctness. title: Transformation of the teaching role through educational automation and intelligent technologies: a systematic review
text_snippet: Transformation of the teaching role through educational automation and intelligent technologies: a systematic review Introduction Educational automation is increasingly used in teaching, but its implications for teachers' tasks, responsibilities, and professional agency remain insufficiently synthesised across educational levels. This review examined how automated and intelligent technologies are transforming the teaching role. Methods Empirical studies indexed in Scopus and Web of Science from 2020 to 2024 were reviewed following PRISMA 2020. Eligibility was structured using PICO, and methodological quality was appraised with the 2018 Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Results Fifty-eight studies met the eligibility and quality threshold: 41 quantitative, eight qualitative, and nine mixed-methods studies. Three domains emerged: teachers' adoption perspectives and constraints; technology-mediated models that redistribute teaching work; and educational outcomes conditioned by teacher competence, institutional support, and governance. Twenty-four studies met five MMAT criteria, 20 met four, and 14 met three. title: iSTEAM and TLIF as frameworks for artistic and mathematical creativity: a comparative conceptual review
text_snippet: iSTEAM and TLIF as frameworks for artistic and mathematical creativity: a comparative conceptual review This article offers a comparative conceptual review of the innovative Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (iSTEAM), and Teaching and Learning Inquiry Framework (TLIF) as two distinct yet complementary pedagogical frameworks for fostering mathematical and artistic creativity. It starts from the premise that creativity in education cannot be adequately understood unless it is examined simultaneously through pedagogical, psychological, philosophical, and aesthetic perspectives. Using an integrative review design, the paper synthesizes empirical studies, theoretical works, and review literature published mainly between 2015 and 2025, with selected earlier sources included to trace the historical development of key concepts. The analysis argues that iSTEAM and TLIF share a common foundation in modern and late-modern educational thought, drawing on inquiry, constructivism, symbolic representation, and reflective judgment. title: Patterns of geometric problem-solving errors among pre-tertiary students across levels of geometric reasoning
text_snippet: Patterns of geometric problem-solving errors among pre-tertiary students across levels of geometric reasoning This study examined pre-tertiary students’ geometric problem-solving performance, the distribution of their errors across Van Hiele levels of geometric reasoning, and the nature of these errors using Newman's Error Hierarchical Model. A descriptive quantitative research design, complemented by qualitative content analysis of students’ written responses, was adopted. The sample comprised 300 final-year students selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a researcher-designed Geometry Problem-Solving Test consisting of twelve open-ended items aligned with the senior high school geometry curriculum. Students’ responses were analysed using frequency and percentage distributions, while error patterns were classified using Newman's framework and mapped onto Van Hiele levels.
